title: POC Weekly Caching Sync - Prefix / KV hit-rate
summary: Weekly POC sync to review prefix/KV cache hit rates, discuss prompt reuse strategies, and define next steps for a 24-48h benchmark and instrumentation improvements.
topics: Next steps for benchmark and pilot ramp
action_items: Avery - Share updated cache dashboard query and raw hit-rate CSV by 2026-10-07
Samir - Run 24h headroom test (ramp to 2k RPS with 50% sustained) and collect per-tenant hit rates by 2026-10-13
Maya - Provide sample prompt corpus (top 10k prompts) and indicate which contain PII by 2026-10-09
Elena - Validate VPC egress rules for prefetching and confirm whether we can enable sticky routing by 2026-10-12
next_steps: Redwood to enable debug-level prefix canonicalization for BrightRetail test cluster
Customer to share anonymized top prompts and success criteria for quality vs latency tradeoff
Schedule 48h run with warmup phase and traffic shaping for corner-case hot keys
transcript: Header: 2026-10-06 10:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Avery, Samir, Jules (Redwood); Maya, Tom, Elena, Noah (BrightRetail)
[00:00] Avery: ok hey everyone thanks for joining um we are on for the caching sync today, quick agenda run through and then dive into the hit rates
[00:12] Maya: yeah thanks, we've been looking at the last week's numbers, hit rates feel low — kv cache is like, uh, 12%? prefix cache around 18% depending on session
[00:30] Samir: got it, those match what we saw on our end, weirdly the traffic shape changed after you enabled dynamic prompts, so reuse dropped
[00:45] Tom: just to flag — we added more personalization tokens so prompts diverge, we thought canonicalization would help but not sure how aggressive to be

[01:05] Samir: right, canonicalization tradeoffs — if we normalize too much we can lose entity-level context. for BrightRetail we saw the biggest wins when normalizing prices and session ids only, not product nouns
[01:35] Maya: can you show the query that computes hit-rate? I want to make sure our counting matches yours

[01:50] Avery: sure i'll share the dashboard link after, short version: prefix hits are where the first N tokens map exactly to a cached KV entry; KV hits are exact key matches after full prompt hashing
[02:10] Jules: note — our auto-ttl for prefix entries is conservative right now, set to 5m, which might evict hot keys during shopping spikes, we can tune that
[02:38] Elena: 5 minutes seems low during flash sales, could we make TTL adaptive based on recent access frequency?
[03:00] Samir: yes we support hot-key lengthening, basically extend TTL when you see repeated hits in window X, we just need to enable it for your cluster and pick thresholds
[03:25] Noah: is there risk of cache poisoning if we extend TTLs? some prompts include user-specific data, we need to avoid serving cached outputs with PII
[03:40] Samir: good point — we have a policy layer that marks prompts with sensitive tokens as non-cacheable. need your tagger to mark those in the sample corpus
[04:05] Maya: we'll annotate top 10k prompts and flag PII, can do by Friday, that should help the non-cache mask
[04:22] Tom: back to hit-rate, curious about prefix length N you're using in production on Redwood Dedicated? is it 16 tokens by default?

[04:35] Avery: default N is 12 tokens for prefix cache, kv use full prompt hash, but we've been experimenting with 8 to 20 depending on typical prompt lengths; for BrightRetail shorter prefixes gave more reuse but less semantic anchoring
[05:00] Maya: we think many of our prompts have long common prefixes like 'Create a product description for' — maybe we should canonicalize that template so prefix hits go way up

[05:18] Samir: exactly, template unfolding — another tactic is prompt deduping on the app side: replace known template shards with token placeholders and then unroll server-side before inference if needed
[05:40] Elena: question — how much of this is safe for our VPC/private cluster? any extra egress for prefetching?
[05:55] Jules: prefetching is in-proxy, doesn't leave VPC, but it can increase compute for warmup. we need infra to allow internal prefetch threads; Elena said she'd check iptables and egress rules
[06:20] Elena: i'll validate and get back, might need a small rule change, low risk but need approval from security
[06:40] Tom: what about measurement? our internal metric shows 18% but Redwood dashboard shows 12% — mismatch in denominator?

[06:55] Avery: likely difference in how we count 'eligible' cacheable requests. we'll send the exact SQL. quick note: we exclude requests with dynamic tools or function calls from hit-rate denominator by default
[07:20] Maya: ah that explains some, we call some external enrichment in prompt pipeline, will try tagging those so they are filtered consistently

[07:36] Samir: on tuning, recommended minimal changes: 1) canonicalize template prefixes, 2) enable hot-key TTL extension, 3) increase prefix length to 14 for the 24h run, 4) run headroom test with ramped traffic
[08:00] Tom: fine, what's the expected jump? if we do those 4 actions what's realistic for hit-rate improvement?
[08:12] Samir: conservative estimate 25-30% total (from 12 to ~40), optimistic 50% if templates cover big fraction of traffic and PII exclusions are low
[08:36] Maya: we care about end-to-end latency too, any cache hit reduces median by ~40-60ms?
[08:50] Samir: yes typical token-latency delta per request is 30-90ms depending on model size and decoding. caching saves both KV lookup and reduces decode length sometimes via prefix completion
[09:10] Avery: also watch for tail latency effects when cache hit spikes cause backend load for cache misses, that's why headroom run is important
[09:30] Jules: instrumentation — we'll add per-tenant heatmaps, request sampling and store raw prompts for a 24h window (anonymized) to debug mismatches, we'll need your ok for data retention period
[09:55] Elena: retention ok for 24h anonymized; security wants PII scrubbed before storage, Maya's annotation will help
[10:10] Tom: are there any config changes that require redeploy vs runtime flags? e.g., enabling hot-key TTL or changing prefix length

[10:25] Samir: both are runtime flags for the most part, prefix length adjustment is config you can flip without rolling infra, TTL adaptive policy can be toggled live, only kernel-level quantization changes require deploys
[10:50] Maya: good, we prefer live toggles for quick iteration in POC
[11:05] Noah: curious about effect on cost — if we increase caching hit-rate, that lowers token compute but prefetch/warm threads add CPU, net should be lower but want a projection
[11:25] Avery: we'll provide projection model — delta cost per 10% hit-rate improvement with current workload and model; we'll include CPU prefetch overhead estimates
[11:40] Samir: note competitor mention — we saw some customers using Bedrock caching layers, but Redwood's prefix+KV integration tends to be simpler for prompt reuse patterns
[11:58] Tom: ok capture that, any risks with canonicalization affecting quality?
[12:12] Samir: small risk — canonicalization can remove signals; we'll test with your eval set and measure BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and A/B on quality targets you provide
[12:30] Maya: we'll send the eval set (1000 items) and the pass/fail criteria, want to iterate overnight if possible

[12:45] Jules: plan: we'll enable debug canonicalization in your test cluster, run a 48h experiment: 12h baseline, 24h tuned, 12h rollback, collect hit-rates, quality metrics, latency and cost. Samir will run headroom ramp within that window.
[13:10] Tom: sounds good, timeline?
[13:18] Avery: target start next Monday 2026-10-12, Samir will kick off the headroom test and Jules will enable instrumentation before start
[13:30] Maya: action items recap please

[13:35] Avery: recap — Redwood shares dashboard and SQL, Samir runs headroom, Jules enables debug canonicalization and instrumentation, BrightRetail shares top prompts and eval set, Elena validates VPC rules. meeting notes and links to dashboard will be emailed after this call
[13:55] Tom: thanks all, we'll sync next week same time, please include outcome of security review in thread
[14:05] Avery: thanks everyone, talk soon — bye
